cards.explanation: The answer is stupid. Proverbs 12:1 says, "…he who hates correction is stupid." It's blunt, and it sits right next to the person who loves discipline and so loves knowledge. Nobody enjoys hearing the timer was set too long, but I'd rather hear it before the batch comes out burnt.

The answer is uprooted. Proverbs 12:3 says, "…the righteous cannot be uprooted." A man can't be established through wickedness, but the righteous stay put. Picture a tree that no wind can pull out of the ground. Proverbs 12:12 comes back to roots, too, saying the root of the righteous flourishes.

The answer is her husband's crown. Proverbs 12:4 says, "A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown…" A crown is something you wear on your head for everyone to see. Friends, I'd say that's about as high a compliment as a proverb can give.

The answer is rescues. Proverbs 12:6 says, "…the speech of the upright rescues them." Look at the two sides of it. The words of the wicked "…lie in wait for blood…" and the words of the upright do the opposite. Same mouth equipment, totally different results.

The answer is False. Proverbs 12:7 says, "The wicked are overthrown and perish, but the house of the righteous will stand." So the house of the righteous stands, it doesn't fall. Notice that little word "but." It's where the verse swings the other way.

The answer is his wisdom. Proverbs 12:8 says, "A man is praised according to his wisdom…" The other side of it is that "…a twisted mind is despised." The proverb isn't asking what's in your wallet, friends. It's asking what's in your head.

The answer is food. Proverbs 12:9 says, "Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food." The self-important man has the big attitude and the empty table. I'll take the full table, friends, and let the attitude go.

The answer is cruelty. Proverbs 12:10 says, "…the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty." The wicked might call it mercy, but the verse says that's all it ever is: cruelty. The righteous man, meanwhile, regards the life of his animal.

The answer is whoever chases fantasies. Proverbs 12:11 says, "The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment." One man is out in the field. The other is out chasing something that isn't there. I think the field man goes home with the better dinner.

The answer is True. Proverbs 12:13 says, "An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble." His own mouth sets the trap for the evil man. The righteous man walks out of trouble instead.

The answer is speech. Proverbs 12:14 says, "By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands returns to him." Both halves of the verse are about what a man does, with his mouth and with his hands. The word that fills in the blank is speech.

The answer is that a wise man listens to counsel. Proverbs 12:15 says, "The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel." The fool is sure he's right. The wise man is willing to hear someone else out.

The answer is that a prudent man overlooks it. Proverbs 12:16 says, "A fool’s anger is known at once, but a prudent man overlooks an insult." The prudent man lets it slide. I've been called a lot of names in my day, friends, and letting some of them go sure beats carrying them around.

The answer is healing. Proverbs 12:18 says, "Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing." Same tongue, two very different results. One cuts and the other mends.
The answer is True. Proverbs 12:19 says, "Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment." Forever on one side and a moment on the other. That's not even a close race.

The answer is joy. Proverbs 12:20 says, "Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but the counselors of peace have joy." Deceit sits in one set of hearts and joy sits in the other. I'd pick the joy every time.
The answer is False. Proverbs 12:21 says, "No harm befalls the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble." So it's the righteous who get no harm. The trouble goes to the wicked.

The answer is those who deal faithfully. Proverbs 12:22 says, "Lying lips are detestable to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight." Think about what that means, friends. The faithful ones bring Him delight.

The answer is diligent. Proverbs 12:24 says, "The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor." The diligent hand rules, and the lazy one ends up working under somebody else. That's a rough swap.

The answer is a good word. Proverbs 12:25 says, "Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up." A good word is what lifts the heart that anxiety weighs down. I've seen a kind word do more for a worn-out stamper than a whole batch of fresh dough.
The answer is True. Proverbs 12:26 says, "A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the ways of the wicked lead them astray." The righteous man is careful. The wicked go astray.

The answer is life. Proverbs 12:28 says, "There is life in the path of righteousness, but another path leads to death." Two paths, and the proverbs close on that note. The chapter ends by pointing to life.
